name: Atlantic puffin
alt: A puffin with a bright orange-red beak and orange feet stands on a lichen-covered rock with both wings raised.
description: More puffins breed in Iceland than anywhere else, and the Westman Islands have the largest colony. They dig burrows in cliff-top soil and dive for sand eels.

name: Arctic tern
alt: An Arctic tern with a black cap and red beak perches on a yellow and white post, with a blurred green field behind it.
habitat: Coasts, gravel flats and grassland near the sea
description: The Arctic tern has the longest migration of any animal, flying between the Arctic and Antarctica every year. It will dive at people who walk too close to its nest.

name: Common guillemot
alt: A dark brown guillemot with a white belly and a thin white line behind its eye swims on calm grey water.
habitat: Narrow ledges on sea cliffs, such as Látrabjarg
season: On the cliffs April to August, at sea the rest of the year
description: Guillemots lay a single egg straight onto a bare cliff ledge. The egg is pointed at one end, so if it gets bumped it rolls in a circle instead of falling off.

name: Rock ptarmigan
alt: A ptarmigan in brown summer feathers with a white belly and a small red patch above its eye stands on grey gravel.
description: The ptarmigan changes colour with the seasons: white in winter to hide in the snow, and mottled brown in summer. It is a traditional Christmas dinner in many Icelandic homes.

name: Greater scaup
alt: A female scaup with a brown body, yellow eye and white patch at the base of its blue-grey beak swims on rippled water, with another duck behind it.
description: Most of Iceland's scaup nest around Lake Mývatn, one of the best duck lakes in Europe. The male has a dark head with a green shine and a pale grey back.

name: Purple sandpiper
alt: A purple sandpiper with speckled grey-brown feathers and yellow-orange legs stands on a rock in front of blue sea.
habitat: Rocky shores in winter, moors and highlands in summer
description: The purple sandpiper is one of the few wading birds that stay in Iceland through the winter. It searches for food on seaweed-covered rocks at the edge of the waves.

name: Whimbrel
alt: A whimbrel with streaked brown feathers walks across frosty grass, holding a tiny insect at the tip of its long, curved beak.
description: A large share of the world's whimbrels breed in Iceland. Its long, down-curved beak and bubbling song are a classic part of the Icelandic summer.

name: Ruddy turnstone
alt: A turnstone with a black-and-white face, orange-brown back and orange legs stands on dark lava rock.
season: Mostly spring and autumn, some stay the winter
description: Turnstones stop in Iceland on their way to and from Greenland and Canada. True to their name, they flip over stones and seaweed to find food underneath.
